params.body:
Four problems a worker ran into on a real fiche:

**The screen stays on.** The screen went off while the fiche was still open. The fiche page (`/werf/fiche`) now holds a screen wake lock. The browser drops the lock whenever the page is hidden, so the page takes it again each time it comes back into view. A browser without wake lock behaves as before. Code: `resources/js/wake-lock.js`, with tests in `tests/js/wake-lock.test.js`.

**A machine or material can be added later.** A machine that came off the fiche could not be put back, for two reasons:
- The question panel offers machines only while the fiche has none.
- `suggestedMachines` and `suggestedArticles` returned nothing once the fiche said "no machines" or "no material".

The board now shows **Machine toevoegen** and **Materiaal toevoegen** (suggestions plus search) whenever he worked on a site, the fiche is not handed in, and that question is not already the open one. Both suggestion lists now ignore the "none" answer. Picking a machine or material still clears it, as it already did.

**The material list is in order.** The list in the correction form ran by name only, so the diameters of one bend came in no order. It is now:
- grouped per catalogue group (`optgroup`);
- the types in natural order (15°, 30°, 45°, 90°), then the diameter from small to large;
- with the diameter written first: `ø110 45° enkele mof`.

This uses the new `Article::pickLabel()`, also used for the tiles, the search results and the board. `label()` is unchanged, so the office, the CSV, the Bouwsoft entry and the conversation see the same text as before.

**The quantity is in its unit.** In the catalogue, "Magere kiftbeton 150 kg/c" is sold per m³, and the 150 kg/c is its strength. The conversation could put 150 in the quantity with "kg/c" as the unit, and the correction form had no way to change the unit. Now:
- Picking an article in the correction form takes that article's catalogue unit.
- A line without an article gets a unit choice next to the quantity.
- The article schema tells the model that kg/c is the strength of concrete and belongs in the description, and that the quantity is in m³.

Checked by screenshot on a copy of the demo database with the catalogue seeded, at 390px and 1280px: the board with the add links, the machine panel open, and the correction form with the unit choice. Tests are in `tests/Feature/WorksheetAddLaterTest.php`. The full suite passes (368/368), the JS tests pass (24/24), and Pint is clean.

No migration.
params.title: Werf fiche: screen stays on, add machines and material later, list in order, quantity in its unit
